text:
mira: seeing a weird spike — multiple accounts with >10 MFA prompts in <30m and fast geo hops reported. detection pipeline flagged impossible-travel pairs and a cascade of session revokes across tenants.

sam: do we have IPs / ASN list?

mira: yes, payload: ASN 6939 + a handful of cloud provider IPs. Sample log: `auth.fail TOTP user=alice@redwood.com src=52.15.200.3 ua=Firefox` then `auth.prompt push user=alice@redwood.com status=sent` repeated 8x.

alejandra: this looks like an MFA fatigue/push bombing pattern. are the targets mostly service accounts or humans?

mira: humans — product, docs, a couple of infra leads. No clear service account pattern.

irene: starting containment: adding src CIDRs to temporary denylist at edge WAF, enabling stricter adaptive rate-limit for auth endpoints. pushing revoke-sessions for affected users.

ryan-oncall: command I ran: `sessionctl revoke --users alice,bob,carla --invalidate-kv=true` — sessions evicted, triggered session-bot confirmation.

session-bot: revoked 18 sessions, queued 4 MFA resets, audit-event ids: ev-8f3a, ev-8f3b.

mira: thanks. can we also block new device registration flows for 1 hour? want to stop fresh enroll attempts.

sam: yes — feature flag `auth.disable_device_reg` set to true in prod via deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: flag updated in prod in 2s, rollout=instant, whoami=deploy-bot.

alejandra: notify affected users with recommended steps (re-enroll MFA, rotate session tokens). Draft for comms? keep it short: "we detected suspicious authentication activity; we revoked active sessions and reset MFA prompts; rotate passwords if you notice anything odd".

mira: +1. also recommending force password reset for the subset that had >5 failed TOTPs.

leah: heads-up to execs: send high-level note, avoid naming tenants publicly. do we have indicators to share with partners (SOCs)?

mira: indicators: list of src IPs, UA strings (headless-chrome variants), ASN. will paste to secure incident ticket.

sam: quick KMS question — some refresh tokens are encrypted client-side before storage. do we need a KMS rotation?

irene: short answer: rotate any long-lived keys that mapped to compromised sessions. I'm running a KMS audit query to list key usage over last 48h. if keys show suspicious use we'll rotate and publish cert rotation plan.

alejandra: also check audit logging retention — we need raw auth logs for 90 days for the RCA. can infra increase retention for the auth-log index?

sam: already bumped to 120d for auth-* indices as a precaution.

mira: triage notes: 1) containment done (denylist + rate-limit + revoke + disable device reg) 2) user comms drafted 3) KMS audit in progress 4) prepare scoped RBAC review for the few infra admins targeted — ensure no lateral escalation.

ryan-oncall: creating incident ticket INC-2023-4477 with runbook link and current artifacts (pcap, logs, indicators). assigning to alejandro for further forensics.

alejandra: post-incident actions: update auth SLOs to include push-flood detection, add threshold alerting, add second-factor challenge quota per account (soft limit).

mira: add note to action items: evaluate automated dampening (temp block after 3 push sends), improve UX for users to decline/pause pushes.

irene: final — will rotate affected service keys if KMS audit shows anomalies and then send an RFC for permanent RBAC tightenings for accounts with admin privileges.

mira: thanks everyone. logging final timeline into the incident ticket and will schedule a 30m RCA in 2 business days.

ryan-oncall: +1, closing the immediate containment channel. will hand off to forensics. :lock:
